title: Typed Cache Tensors Design Review, Round 4
eyebrow: Round-4 review of the third codex revision of the design for issue #4525 (positron-ai/tron)
h1: Did the third revision close the round-3 findings, and is the typed KV-cache tensor design implementable now?
meta: Reviewed 2026-09-22 UTC by Claude (Fable 5.1) for jhan. Design reviewed: [status/design-new-tensor-type.html](design-new-tensor-type.html), third revision by codex after the [round-3 review](claude-review-design-new-tensor-type-r3.html) (finalized 2026-09-22 16:43 UTC, 168,971 bytes, sha256 d2e9dabf). Sources pinned to main f46e48ba (the design's snapshot), main 2880c3aa9b (the tip the design's S15-S21 cite), the live main tip 0a51385e95 (fetched 2026-09-22 17:05 UTC; one inserted line in model.hpp since 2880c3aa9b, nothing else among the design's files) and PR 4424 head 30c4ac82cb.
short_version: The third revision resolved 71 of the 79 open items (52 round-3 findings plus 27 residuals from earlier rounds). 8 are partly resolved, each a one-sentence wording gap; none is unresolved and none regressed.

This round found 47 new defects: 1 major, 11 minor, 35 notes. The major one is a process gap, not a design error: the design demands proof that the required Test host job executed the new tests before a test is committed, a draft pull request runs no Test host job, and the page names no route to that evidence (J01). One new sentence on the production write path is wrong (the model's V buffer carries dma = true, not false; J09); it cannot produce wrong bytes, but it must change.

Verdict: accept with minor edits, implementable now. All three judges say so; two ask for the J01 paragraph before the first test commit. After that paragraph and the one-sentence edits listed in section 7, another agent can build the parent from this page.

words: tron
the inference program under test; its source is the positron-ai/tron repository
PR 4424, the child

the open draft pull request "VNNI K: store the K cache of 128-dimension heads in the AMX VNNI layout, with a shared block save" (branch jhan-amx-vnniK, head 30c4ac82cb). After the new parent PR exists, PR 4424 is rebased onto it and is then called the child
the parent PR
the new pull request that issue #4525 asks for: typed access to the existing V and K caches on main, with no new layout
Ben, the reviewer

the tron maintainer who reviewed PR 4424 on 2026-09-21 (a worker-index question, a review asking for typed tensors, and an API sketch). The design calls him "the reviewer" and, since this revision, no longer names him
issue #4525
the GitHub issue codex created for the parent PR; jhan edited its title and first sentence on 2026-09-22 00:10 UTC; unchanged since
KV cache, K, V
the saved key (K) and value (V) vectors of earlier tokens; attention reads them
page, slot, head, D

a page holds 64 token positions; a slot is the cache region of one layer (or of several layers that share it); a head is one attention head; D is the head size, the number of values per token per head (128 for PR 4424's models)
bf16
the 16-bit brain floating-point format used for cached K and V
AMX, AVX-512, 16-lane and 8-lane builds

AMX and AVX-512 are CPU instruction sets. tron's vector width TRON_CHUNK_SIZE is 16 fp32 values with AVX-512 (the 16-lane build) and 8 without (the 8-lane build); the 8-lane build stores V row-major, so it has no pair-interleaved V
packed V (pair-interleaved V)
today's V storage in the 16-lane build: for each dimension, tokens 2p and 2p+1 sit next to each other. Element offset = (token/2)*(2*D) + 2*dim + token%2
native K
today's K storage: one token's D values consecutive in memory (row-major)
blocked packed K (VNNI K)

PR 4424's K storage for 128-dimension heads: two consecutive dimensions of one token share a 4-byte unit, and 16 tokens share one 64-byte line; a 16-token by 32-dimension panel is one AMX tile of 1,024 bytes
expr, view, const_view, tensor

tron's expression interface (h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp), its typed pointer views over regularly laid-out memory and their read-only form (h/tron/tensor/view.hpp, views.hpp), and its owning arrays (h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp)
kv_block
the struct that holds K then V for one head of one slot in one page (h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp)
set_v, get_v, append_v, scaled_v, v_data, v_base

today's V functions in kv_cache.hpp: write one token, read one token, copy one token between pages, compute the weighted V sum, and return the raw pointer of a V plane (the last two are removed by the design)
scaled_v_expr

detail::scaled_v_expr, the expression in kv_cache.hpp that computes the weighted V sum; its 16-lane constructor loads whole 64-byte pair tiles with _mm512_load_si512 and multiplies them with _mm512_dpbf16_ps
save_v_impl
the model function (h/tron/models/model.hpp) that stores one token's V into the cache during a forward pass; it calls page::set_v
Zero-Initialized V Slots invariant

the rule in kv_cache.hpp (Note [Zero-Initialized V Slots], lines 2055-2065) that every even-token V write zeroes its odd partner row. The weighted sum reads a whole pair even when the token count is odd, and NaN times 0 is NaN, so the padding row must be zero
arena, book

an arena is one allocated memory region holding cache blocks; book is the class that owns the arenas and the pages; kv_blocks_alias is the base pointer the uniform-reclaimability accessor indexes across slots
EAGLE
the speculative model; its cache adds one extra physical KV slot at the end of the retained arena and a separate embedding buffer (x_data) that holds no kv_block; it requires uniform geometry
GOF, page_info

group of four: four tokens of K and V staged for the FPGA's hardware KV cache; the staging code reaches a page's rows through the page_info callbacks in h/tron/gof.hpp (namespace tron::hardware); the V callback (v_head_fn in h/tron/scheduler/full.hpp) unpacks one row into caller-owned scratch
CI, Nix test build, TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, TRON_K_VNNI, TRON_AMX_DISABLE

CI is the automated build and test. The Nix test build is the required CI lane (workflow gcp-nix.yml). TRON_AMX_DISPATCH and TRON_K_VNNI are CMake options that compile the AMX attention kernels and PR 4424's K layout; the Nix lane sets neither. TRON_AMX_DISABLE=1 is an environment variable that makes an AMX build take the non-AMX path; it is read once per process. Issue #3997 tracks the AMX gap
Slice, logs-<host>/run-NNNN, test-cost records

bin/slice is the repository's test scheduler. It writes one log per test binary under <checkout>/logs-<runner hostname>/run-NNNN and keeps at most 10 such directories. config/test-benchmarks.json holds one duration and memory record per test and platform block (genoa96, genoa32, granite_rapids_6960p, granite_rapids_6962p); bin/slice bench --update or --new refreshes them, bin/slice bench --check only reports missing records
lint-notes, lint-toolchain, Note [Name]

make lint-notes runs the checker for the repository's documentation Notes (a Note [Name] heading underlined with ~~~, referenced as See Note [Name]). The required Lint job builds the Nix check lint-toolchain, which ends with make lint-notes
the generator, TronCpp.hs, LoopyTronSpec.hs

ingest/src/TronCpp.hs is the Haskell program that emits the model C++ (run() for the main thread, run_main_help for helper threads); ingest/test/LoopyTronSpec.hs asserts the generated call text; bin/ingest-cabal test runs those tests and the required Test ingest job runs them in CI

the file /bill-has-instance-0,2 on delphi-3bda; when present, another user may use the first half of the machine (tron --instance 0,2); jhan's harness always runs on the second half and never changes it; exec/bill-share.sh take/release removes and restores it

v_vnni_tensor, v_vnni_view, v_vnni_row, detail::v_vnni_access

the design's names for the packed-V owner (the aligned array inside the cache block), the typed rank-2 view over it, its logical row expression, and the helper in h/tron/tensor/v_vnni.hpp that alone may return the packed pointer; the design permits typed V operations, weights_times_v_128x4 and scaled_v_expr to use it
append_v_row, load_row, copy_token

the design's typed bulk operations: write one token's V row into the packed plane (an even token zeroes its odd partner), read one row out, copy one token between planes. append_v_row is the design's name for the sketch's V store_row. The design adds no copy_plane for V
kv_cache_fwd.hpp, v_vnni.hpp, k_vnni.hpp

the design's new headers under h/tron/tensor/: a declarations-only header (no intrinsics) that amx_attn_iface.hpp includes, the V definitions header, and the child's K definitions header (the child's existing h/tron/kernels/k_vnni.hpp keeps only qk_group)
native_k_view, const_native_k_view
the design's new aliases for today's row-major K view types; const_native_k_view<64, 128> becomes the K parameter of qk_rowmajor_128x4
page::v_packed, page::k_packed
the design's read-only accessors returning the packed V view (parent, 16-lane build only) and the packed K view (child)
t_amx_numerics, bf16_rne, qk_inputs

the test t/t_amx_numerics.cpp that compares the real AMX kernels with scalar references; bf16_rne is its round-to-nearest-even helper; qk_inputs is its 64-byte-aligned K and Q fixture struct; its PV case builds the packed V page by hand in a std::vector today

draft gating, Run CI, ready_for_review

in the required GCP Nix workflow the product jobs (Build ingest, Build model traces, Prepare Tron build inputs, and through them Build Tron, Test host, Test FPGA and Test) run for a pull request only when it is not a draft or carries the Run CI label; a draft pull request runs only the Lint, CI machinery and Fresh Cabal plan jobs. ready_for_review is the GitHub event that fires when a draft is promoted; it is one of the workflow's pull_request triggers
dmatensor, btensor, host executor

dmatensor is tron's owning array in DMA-safe memory (h/tron/hardware/dmatensor.hpp); its views carry dma = true. hardware::btensor is the bf16 dmatensor the tp1, tp2 and tp4 executors use for the model's V buffer. The host executor uses a plain tensor whose views carry dma = false; t_llama_unit's model cases use that executor

dispositions.assessment:
The design adopts round-3 option A, the verifiers' default, and states the reason (the expression counts as a V-specific kernel). Every part of the corrected recommendation is in the body: placement in kv_cache.hpp (:286, :346, :390), the read-only packed view as the 16-lane constructor input (:286, :390), the pair-tile base obtained once through the helper (:286, :346, :390), the preserved _mm512_load_si512 / _mm512_dpbf16_ps loop with unrolling and addition order (:286, :390), and the helper row naming scaled_v_expr as the only kv_cache.hpp user while page methods, book and tests do not call it (:260). The step-2 placement sentence the round-3 edit had deleted is restored (:390; design-wdiff.txt INSERT @old 5884).

Facts checked against the source:
- scaled_v_expr is inside namespace detail in kv_cache.hpp: `namespace detail {` at kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1987, `struct scaled_v_expr final` at :1990. RIGHT.
- The 16-lane constructor loop is `_mm512_dpbf16_ps(tN, _mm512_load_si512(tile + N), scale)` with tiles t0..t3 for head 64 (:2087-2090) and t0..t7 for head 128 (:2102-2109); the bound is `end = (count + 1) / 2 * 2` at :2078. The design's loop, unrolling, and packed-bound statements are RIGHT.
- The constructor already keeps `const bf16s* const data` as a member (:1992) and derives each pair tile from it (:2085-2086, :2100-2101), so obtaining the base once through the helper and keeping the loop is implementable without changing the instruction stream.
- page::scaled_v passes `count()` as the live count (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2260-2261); page::count() is at :1492-1494. "live count from page::count()" RIGHT.
- "the only user in kv_cache.hpp" holds: set_v, get_v and append_v forward to typed operations in v_vnni.hpp (design :266-270, :281-285); the 16-lane copy_storage_slot branch copies V by calling append_v per token (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1944-1946); fill_storage_slot keeps its whole-block cast as the documented exception (:1371; design :274); page::v_packed returns a view from the owner (design :284).
- "tests do not call it": the fake weights_times_v_128x4 at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:185-188 leaves its input parameter unnamed and only fills the output, so a typed fake needs no pointer. RIGHT.
- Precedent: Ben's sketch defines detail::vnni_access reading view.data_ and says "Ordinary cache and attention code should not use it" (github-review.json, comment 5765866077 body lines 153-166) and "kernels extract the pointer once and retain the existing instruction sequence" (line 210). The design's option-A text matches that precedent.
- Section 9 :553 matches the body text.

votes.reason: The design adopts round-3 option A in the body text, not only in section 9. The helper row names detail::scaled_v_expr as a permitted user of detail::v_vnni_access, calls it "the only user in kv_cache.hpp", classifies it as a V-specific kernel, and says page methods, book and tests do not call the helper [design-r4.txt:260]. The page::scaled_v row says the expression stays in kv_cache.hpp, obtains the pair-tile base (the address of the first 64-byte load of a token pair) once through the helper, and preserves the _mm512_load_si512 and _mm512_dpbf16_ps loop, tile unrolling and addition order [design-r4.txt:286]. Section 6 and step 2 repeat placement and mechanism [design-r4.txt:346, :390]. The new row does all of this. It drops the make BUILD_TYPE=Debug path and the "Plain Make defaults" sentence (both present at design-r3.txt:455, absent at design-r4.txt:482), prescribes cmake --build plus gen/t_llama_unit with filters, states the stamp fact, forbids switching an existing tree through a Make variable, and requires both checks. Checked facts: (1) GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:80 `BUILD_TYPE := RelWithDebInfo`; the gen/config/test rule at :538-543 depends on $(CMAKELISTS), config/models.yaml, t/proxy/ctest-trampoline.sh, $(FUSE_STATS_STAMP), $(PRESET_STAMP) and the plugin-bundle stamps, and runs `cmake --preset $(CMAKE_PRESET) -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$(BUILD_TYPE) ...`; the FUSE stamp tracks ENABLE_FUSE_STATS (:289-290) and the preset stamp tracks CMAKE_PRESET (:299-303). No stamp or prerequisite tracks BUILD_TYPE, so "Make's configuration stamp does not track BUILD_TYPE" is right. (2) :880-881 `gen/t_%: gen/config/test $(HEADERS) $(SOURCES)` runs cmake --build; :886-887 `t_%: gen/t_%` runs `gen/$@` with no arguments, so running gen/t_llama_unit directly with filters is the right way to select cases. (3) TRON_IGNORE_NAN is passed as the compile option `-DTRON_IGNORE_NAN` under `$<NOT:$<CONFIG:Debug>>` (src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295 and :314-318), so it is absent from Debug compile lines and visible in compile_commands.json; CMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS is "1" in the base-ninja preset (CMakePresets.json@2880c3aa9b:22), which the native preset inherits (:31-39, binaryDir gen, CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE RelWithDebInfo). (4) CMAKE_RUNTIME_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY is CMAKE_BINARY_DIR (CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:66) and add_catch_test calls add_executable("${TEST_NAME}" ...) (t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:189), so the target name t_llama_unit and the path gen/t_llama_unit are right. (5) The S17 link [Make test configuration] points at GNUmakefile#L538-L543, the gen/config/test rule. Right. Two parts of the corrected text are not repeated: the list of inputs that trigger a reconfigure (CMakeLists.txt, models.yaml, preset input) and the note that make t_<name> runs the whole binary. Neither is load-bearing now: the row no longer uses any Make target, :476 warns that Make targets may reconfigure gen/, and the CMakeCache.txt check catches a reconfigure before the run. Small wording note, no change needed: the cache file line is `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE:STRING=Debug`; the row's "CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug" is a readable paraphrase.

Section 9, design-r4.txt:565 "| G22 | Give the PV numerics fixture an aligned typed V owner. Fill it through typed operations, pass its read-only view, and compare bytes copied out against the independent packing formula. State the fixture policy for hand-packed input bytes. [Numerics fixture] [Parent test migration] | Run the real numerics case. A signature-only fake cannot prove the packed fixture is correct. |"
dispositions.assessment:
The corrected recommendation (design-text and intent lenses) asked the design to say that the PV case's std::vector page moves into a v_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64, HEAD_SIZE_128> owner (16,384 bytes, 64-byte aligned), which public fill route to use, that owner.as_view() is the kernel argument, that the pair-formula check runs on bytes copied out of the owner, whether a memcpy of hand-packed bytes into the owner is allowed, and that the QK case keeps an explicit const_native_k_view wrap. The body text at design-r4.txt:399-403 states every one of these. Step 6 (design-r4.txt:394) points to that section, so the fix is in the body and not only in section 9. The section-9 row (design-r4.txt:565) matches the body.

Facts checked in the fix:
- The hand-packed page exists as described. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:199 declares the logical input `std::vector<float> v(PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128)`. Line 203 declares `std::vector<tron::bf16> v_page(...)`. Lines 204-211 fill it with the pair formula through `tron::bf16::from_bits(bf16_rne(...))`. Lines 226-227 pass `v_page.data()` to weights_times_v_128x4. Lines 238-239 read v_page back by the same formula for the reference. So the design's "hand-packed std::vector<bf16> kernel input" and "independent pair-interleave formula" are right.
- bf16_rne is an existing test helper. t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@2880c3aa9b:42-47 defines `uint16_t bf16_rne(float f)` with round-to-nearest-even. The design's definition "round a float to bf16 using nearest-even rounding" is right.

"Preserve or link ... explicitly" at :496 covers "attach or link them in the PR".

"Logs: <checkout>/logs-<hostname>/run-NNNN" is RIGHT.

So a CI job log carries one result line per test binary. RIGHT (this follows the lead note, which corrected the intent verifier's "no test names").
- Final counts: bin/slice:4545-4549 prints "{passed} passed, {skipped} skipped, {failed} failed  •  makespan ...". RIGHT.
- Case lines only in files: bin/slice:3148 log_path = run_dir / f"{name}.log"; :3174 open(log_path, "w"); :3182-3187 Popen(stdout=log_f, stderr=STDOUT). RIGHT.
- Upload only on failure: gcp-nix.yml:580-587 "Upload Slice test logs", if: failure() && env.RUN_TESTS == 'true', path ${{ github.workspace }}/logs-*/run-*. RIGHT.
- Store paths: gcp-nix.yml:545 step name "Restore exact Nix test runtime"; bin/ci/tron-build/test_runtime.py:133-136 prints "Preparing test runtime: {canonical_build}; environment={canonical_environment}". RIGHT.
- Next checkout cleans: the Test host and Test FPGA jobs check out with actions/checkout@de0fac2e and only fetch-depth: 0 [gcp-nix.yml:539-541, :606-608]; action.yml at de0fac2e lines 57-59 (read via gh api) defines clean with default true = "git clean -ffdx && git reset --hard HEAD"; .gitignore:68 lists logs-*/, and -x removes ignored paths. RIGHT.
- 10 run directories: bin/slice:114 RETENTION = 10; :2766-2768 prunes while len(existing) >= RETENTION. RIGHT.
- Runner pool: gcp-nix.yml:534 runs-on [self-hosted, fpga, test, avx512]. "Set up job" is GitHub's own first step of every job (facts-r4).

The token loop at 2109-2115 (k_vnni::gather_row then k_vnni::scatter_row) is what "typed K token copies" replaces. The native branch at 2117-2126 is unchanged by the fix, as asked. dispositions.new_defect: Claim: "Retain the existing array copy in the native branch" (design-r4.txt:434) describes the native branch as an array copy. The native branch at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2118-2126 computes `k_size = geometry.head_size * sizeof(bf16)`, takes `k_at(src_begin).data` and `k_at(dst_begin).data`, and runs `memcpy(dst, src, count * k_size)`. It copies `count` token rows starting at the given offsets, not the K array. The word "existing" anchors the meaning, so an implementer is unlikely to replace it with a whole-array assignment. Recommendation: write "Retain the existing row-range memcpy in the native branch."

dispositions.design_evidence: design-r4.txt:432 "| page::set_k_row , page::get_k_row | Use const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for save and view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,seq<D>,sseq<1>> for load. The boolean template arguments preserve the caller's alignment and DMA properties. Preserve the existing gather/scatter instructions. These K routines do not acquire V's stronger alignment requirement. Wrap scratch without copying. Call typed store_row / load_row . Construct read-only source views explicitly in model save paths, copy paths, and affected test callers. Template deduction does not use the conversion from a writable view or raw pointer to const_view . |" The V rule it mirrors: design-r4.txt:270 "Explicitly construct read-only source views where template deduction would otherwise see writable views." Section 9: :573 "Construct read-only K source views explicitly where deduction cannot apply a conversion. [Typed row operations] [Packed accessors] [K caller migration]".
dispositions.assessment: The mechanism is now stated and is right. In h/tron/tensor/view.hpp@2880c3aa9b the rank-1 const_view is `final` (:361), its pointer constructor is `explicit const_view(T const* data = nullptr)` (:373-374), and its constructors from `view` are non-template converting constructors (:382-386). Template argument deduction matches P = const_view<bf16,Aligned,Dma,...> against the argument type with only derived-to-base and qualification adjustments, so a `view` or a `bf16*` argument fails to deduce Aligned and Dma. The rule "construct read-only source views explicitly in model save paths ... and affected test callers" is present. What is missing against the corrected recommendation: all three verifiers and the original recommendation named the callers, and the design names none. The case every verifier called the real gap is not named: `kout`, the writable slice view returned by row_of (h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2861-2864), whose `.data` is passed to set_k_row at :2920, and the raw scratch `conv[0]` passed at :2924. The test files are not named: t/t_llama_unit.cpp has 32 lines calling set_k_row or get_k_row at 30c4ac82cb, t/t_k_vnni_layout.cpp has 8 (for example :401 `page->set_k_row(SLOT_0, 0, tok, row.data())`), t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp has 1 (:101 `zero.data()`). The uniform-geometry forwarding overloads at h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@30c4ac82cb:1752-1764 still take `const bf16* row` and `bf16* row`, and the design does not say they change to the typed views (source lens item 2). The load side is unchanged and right: "Wrap scratch without copying" covers full.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2655 `get_k_row<hw_kv>(slot, kv_head, off, dest)`. "copy paths" was kept although the intent lens asked to remove it (see the new defect). Severity of the finding was note, so the missing names are low risk, but the text does not yet carry what the corrected recommendation asked.

(2) The test fixtures pass alignas(64) float arrays or std::array data() [t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:1919-1923, 2037-2038, 2701-2705, 2759-2761, 2789-2792, 2823-2824; t/heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp@2880c3aa9b:441-444]. dma = false RIGHT. So vs[ix].as_view() carries dma = true in every production executor. Only `host = make_llm_executor<false, tensor, tensor, tensor>` [common.hpp:100] yields dma = false [h/tron/tensor/tensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:35, :71-77]. design-r4.txt:220 "| Blocked packed K | ((((dimension / 32) * (R / 16) + token / 16) * 16 + (dimension % 32) / 2) * 16 + token % 16) * 2 + dimension % 2 | PR #4424 only. Keep the existing layout-selection condition. Keep the kernel restricted to 64 tokens × 128 dimensions. |"

design-r4.txt:222 "R is the stored token count. D is the stored dimension count. The packed-K formula uses groups of 32 dimensions and groups of 16 tokens. Each 16-token by 32-dimension panel is one AMX B tile. Let s = dimension / 32 and c = token / 16. Its base is (s * (R / 16) + c) * 512 bf16 elements. Inside it, use the packed-V formula on a 32-row by 16-column plane with row dimension % 32 and column token % 16. The in-panel offset is ((dimension % 32) / 2) * 32 + 2 * (token % 16) + dimension % 2 bf16 elements. Across the plane, dimension groups are outermost and token blocks are next. confirmed.title: Draft parent runs no Test host job; the required execution evidence has no stated route
confirmed.section: 8. CI ownership and execution evidence (design-r4.txt:494-497); 3. Add the tensor interface to main first (:167); 8. Build configurations (:485); Definition of done (:535-536)
confirmed.claim: The GCP Nix product pipeline does not run for a draft pull request unless it carries the Run CI label. The jobs Build ingest, Build model traces and Prepare Tron build inputs each carry the condition `github.event_name != 'pull_request' || !github.event.pull_request.draft || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'Run CI')`. Build Tron needs Prepare Tron build inputs, and Test host needs Build Tron. So a draft parent without Run CI has no Test host job at all. The design requires required-suite execution evidence before committing a new test (:495). It forbids the Run CI label without user direction (:167, :495). It places gates 'before leaving draft' (:485, :536) and makes 'Required tests collect and execute new behavior coverage with the named evidence' a completion condition (:535). It never states when that evidence can exist. It can exist only after the parent is marked ready for review (the pull_request trigger includes ready_for_review, and the stack rule permits ready-for-review for the PR based on main) or after a user-directed Run CI label. The design also names no local way to verify 'collection' before that point. An implementing agent following :495 on a draft parent cannot obtain the evidence and is told not to use the only label that would produce it. A float load_row that is a moved loop follows that sentence literally. The finding's fix (load_row calls the generic expression-assignment path) departs from the letter of the sketch. The departure is harmless because the float path has no production caller, but it is not something Ben asked for. Round 3 already recorded this duplication risk: G13's lead recommendation allowed "copy ... or hoist", and its verifier correction asked that chunk(i) "reuse one iteration of the load_row loop". The design chose copy [design-r4.txt:262, :558]. That is a permitted choice, so J08 records a maintainability preference, not a defect that must change before implementation.

The finding's own instruction-comparison addition would detect a miss, so this is a narrowing, not a refutation.

confirmed.title: Child VNNI QK identity case: its raw-plane fixture migration is not specified
confirmed.section: 7. Then adapt PR #4424 / Child storage and access (design-r4.txt:409-443); 8. Child only row (:470); 8. Prove real AMX execution (:508); compare the parent's fixture rules at :397-403
confirmed.claim: The child's t_amx_numerics has a VNNI QK identity case (a test that compares qk_vnni_128x4 scores with qk_rowmajor_128x4 scores bit for bit). It holds the K plane in a raw struct, fills it with k_vnni::scatter_row through a raw pointer in a scrambled token order, and passes the raw pointer to qk_vnni_128x4. Under the design, qk_vnni_128x4 takes k_vnni_view<const bf16,64,128> by value (:418, :434), and the K owner and views have no public raw-pointer constructor (:428 applies the V rules of :259 to K). So this case cannot compile as written. The design gives fixture rules for the parent's PV case (:399-403) and for t_k_vnni_layout (:443). It names the child's identity case only for the AMX-proof log rule (:508). It never says how its fixture migrates: which owner, which fill route, whether the scrambled store order is kept, and that the row-major call wraps in->k in const_native_k_view like the parent's QK case.
confirmed.design_quote: The child applies this rule to its packed-K QK identity case.
confirmed.evidence: t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@30c4ac82cb:188-243: `struct alignas(64) vnni_plane { tron::bf16 v[PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]; }` (:210-212); `tron::k_vnni::scatter_row(plane->v, tok, in->k + tok * HEAD_SIZE_128)` in scrambled order with SCRAMBLE_STRIDE_37 and SCRAMBLE_OFFSET_11 (:208-209, :217-219); `qk_rowmajor_128x4(in->k, q_packed, ...)` (:228-229); `qk_vnni_128x4(plane->v, q_rows, ...)` (:230-231); the case sits inside `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` (:22-318) and returns after a WARN when available() is false (:199-202). Design: :418 and :434 (typed qk_vnni_128x4 parameter); :428 ('Apply the V owner's lvalue-only as_view(), const conversion, and private packed-pointer rules to K too'); :259 ('no public raw-pointer constructor'); :399-403 (parent fixture rules); :443 (child rule for t_k_vnni_layout only); :470; :508. Round-3 G22 asked the same question for the parent's PV case and the design answered it at :397-403; no child counterpart exists. Merge note: single candidate, minor kept.
confirmed.recommendation: Add one bullet after :443: 'The child's VNNI QK identity case in t/t_amx_numerics.cpp (30c4ac82cb:188-243) replaces its raw vnni_plane struct with a k_vnni_tensor<PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128> owner (16,384 bytes, 64-byte aligned, heap or local). Fill it with 64 typed K store_row calls, each source row in->k + tok * HEAD_SIZE_128 wrapped explicitly in const_view<bf16,true,false,seq<HEAD_SIZE_128>,sseq<1>> (qk_inputs is alignas(64) and each row is 256 bytes), keeping the scrambled token order (stride 37, offset 11). Pass owner.as_view() to qk_vnni_128x4. Wrap in->k in const_native_k_view<PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128> for the qk_rowmajor_128x4 call, as the parent's QK case does. Fill the owner only through the typed store_row; add no test-only pointer constructor or friend. votes.reason: The central claim holds. The child test case "AMX QK from the VNNI K plane is bit-identical to AMX QK from row-major K" spans t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@30c4ac82cb:188-243. It declares `struct alignas(64) vnni_plane { tron::bf16 v[PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]; }` at :210-212. It fills the plane with `tron::k_vnni::scatter_row(plane->v, tok, in->k + tok * HEAD_SIZE_128)` at :219 in the scrambled order of :217-218 (constants SCRAMBLE_STRIDE_37 and SCRAMBLE_OFFSET_11 at :208-209). It calls `qk_rowmajor_128x4(in->k, q_packed, ...)` at :228-229 and `qk_vnni_128x4(plane->v, q_rows, ...)` at :230-231. The case sits under `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` (:22, `#else` at :318) and returns after a WARN when available() is false (:199-202). Main at 2880c3aa9b has no such case (git grep "bit-identical" finds nothing), so the case is child-only. Under the design, qk_vnni_128x4 takes k_vnni_view<const bf16,PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128> by value [design-r4.txt:418, :434]. Owners and views expose no public raw-pointer constructor [:259], and :428 applies "the V owner's lvalue-only as_view(), const conversion, and private packed-pointer rules to K too"; :431 says packed access derives from k.as_view(); :465 says tests reject raw-pointer construction of packed matrices. The typed K store_row and its pair_base / pair_row_offsets helpers move to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp [:416], so the raw scatter_row call also disappears. The design's fixture rules cover only the parent's PV and QK cases [:399-403] and the child's t_k_vnni_layout [:443]. The identity case is named once, at :508, for the AMX-proof log rule only. The "Child only" row says "Retain layout, shared-save, and AMX numerical cases" [:470] without a fixture route, and :420 says "Include t_amx_numerics if materially changed" without saying what changes. A search of design-r4.txt for identity / scatter_row / vnni_plane / scrambl finds no other relevant line. So the omission is real. The recommendation's facts check out: qk_inputs is alignas(64) with k as its first member (:66-67), each K row is 128 bf16 = 256 bytes, so every row start is 64-byte aligned; the 16,384-byte owner matches :428; the const_native_k_view wrap for qk_rowmajor_128x4 matches :403; the bit comparison is at :233-241. Severity minor matches round-3 G22 (the parent's PV counterpart, graded minor with the correction "a route was derivable, the gap was which route"): an implementer can derive the route from :399-403 and :443, but the design should name it, the scrambled order decision, and the row-major wrap.

votes.reason: The central claim holds. The design names the child's VNNI QK identity case exactly once, at design-r4.txt:508, and only for the AMX-proof log rule ("The child applies this rule to its packed-K QK identity case"). A grep of design-r4.txt for "identity", "scramble" and "vnni_plane" finds no other mention. The child section's fixture rules cover t_k_vnni_layout only (design-r4.txt:443: "Adapt t_k_vnni_layout to actual aligned owners. Fill poison with 64 typed row saves."), and the parent fixture rules at :399-403 are scoped to the parent's PV and QK cases (":401 Do not copy hand-packed input bytes into the owner in these fixtures"). The "Child only" verification row says only "Retain layout, shared-save, and AMX numerical cases" (:470). The source facts are right: t/t_amx_numerics.cpp@30c4ac82cb:210-212 defines `struct alignas(64) vnni_plane { tron::bf16 v[PAGE_TOKENS_64 * HEAD_SIZE_128]; }`, :217-219 fill it with `tron::k_vnni::scatter_row(plane->v, tok, in->k + tok * HEAD_SIZE_128)` in the order tok = (i*37 + 11) % 64, :228-229 call `qk_rowmajor_128x4(in->k, q_packed, ...)`, :230-231 call `qk_vnni_128x4(plane->v, q_rows, ...)`, and the case sits between `#ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH` at :22 and `#else` at :318. The child's current declaration is `void qk_vnni_128x4(const bf16* k_vnni_plane, const bf16* q_rows, float* s, size_t s_stride_floats) noexcept` (h/tron/kernels/amx_attn_iface.hpp@30c4ac82cb:251-254). The design replaces that pointer with `k_vnni_view<const bf16,PAGE_TOKENS_64,HEAD_SIZE_128>` by value (design-r4.txt:418, :434), applies the V no-public-raw-pointer rules to K (:428 with :259), and says the kernel header "keeps only qk_group" after the typed store_row and its helpers move to h/tron/tensor/k_vnni.hpp (:416-417). So both the `scatter_row(plane->v, ...)` call and the `qk_vnni_128x4(plane->v, ...)` call stop compiling. The general child rule "using its old diff as the specification" (:411) cannot fill the gap, because the design itself overrides these interfaces. The route IS derivable from the design (k_vnni_tensor owner :426-428, typed store_row :416 and :432, as_view() :428, view-by-value :434, the sister fixture rule :443), so this is the same shape as round-3 G22 (a permitted route was derivable; the gap was which route), which the round-3 lead graded minor. Severity minor: the ambiguity is confined to a test fixture, the production code is unaffected, and the worst plausible wrong choice is a hand-packed fill through k_vnni::index plus a memcpy into the trivially copyable owner, which would silently change what the case verifies (the test's own comment at :193-196 says it checks "the K store (k_vnni::scatter_row) plus the kernel's panel addressing"), not break the build.

confirmed.title: Native-branch K copy is called an array copy; it is a row-range memcpy
confirmed.section: 7. Child storage and access, Copy and score readers row (design-r4.txt:434)
confirmed.claim: The row says to use defaulted owner assignment for the packed whole-page copy and then to 'Retain the existing array copy in the native branch'. The native branch (the row-major K layout branch of copy_storage_slot) does not copy an array. It computes k_size = head_size * sizeof(bf16), takes k_at(src_begin).data and k_at(dst_begin).data, and runs memcpy(dst, src, count * k_size). It copies count token rows from the given offsets, so a partial token range copies only that range. Placed right after the owner-assignment sentence, 'array copy' reads as a whole-array copy. The K member in that branch is a C array (bf16s k[page_size][head_size / chunk_size]) and cannot be assigned, so a wrong reading fails to compile rather than silently copying the wrong tokens. The word 'existing' anchors the meaning. The wording is inexact but low risk.

The central claim does not hold for an implementer reading the page, for three reasons.

(1) The design already states the precise rule the finding says is missing. Section 6 says: "Preserve native-K and 8-lane V row-range byte copies, packed-V token copies in all four parity combinations, page-boundary splitting, overlap restrictions, and completion-state copying." [design-r4.txt:376]. "Row-range byte copies" for native K is exactly the memcpy of count rows the finding describes. Section 7 restates that rule in short form and relies on it.

(2) "Array" in the section-7 row is the design's name for the native storage branch, not a statement about the extent of the copy. The storage block calls the native type `native_k_storage = bf16s[page_size][head_size / chunk_size]` with the comment "Existing array shape is retained for native K" [design-r4.txt:426]. The next paragraph says "Constrain native k_view() and k_at() to the array branch" [design-r4.txt:428]. So "Retain the existing array copy in the native branch" [design-r4.txt:434] reads as "keep the existing copy code of the array-typed branch", in parallel with "Use defaulted owner assignment" for the owner-typed branch. That is the intended and correct reading. The alternative reading, "copy the whole array", requires ignoring both "retain" and "existing".

The finding concedes this: "The word 'existing' anchors the meaning", a wrong reading "fails to compile rather than silently copying the wrong tokens", and "The wording is inexact but low risk".

confirmed.section: 7. AMX numerics fixture migration (design-r4.txt:401; mirrored for the child at :443)
confirmed.claim: Round-3 G22's lead note and intent verifier asked the design to state whether a test may copy hand-packed bytes into the trivially copyable owner, and said to prefer the append route. The round-4 text turns that into a prohibition for 'these fixtures'. The byte copy is the smallest change to the PV case: one memcpy of 16,384 bytes into a v_vnni_tensor<64,128> and owner.as_view() at the kernel call, with the existing hand-packed std::vector, bf16_rne inputs and reference untouched. It also keeps the case's stated purpose, kernel numerics against an independent input, separate from the write path. The chosen route makes the PV numerics case depend on append_v_row, which the t_llama_unit 'V append and padding' row already covers, and adds 64 aligned bf16_rne source rows, 64 append calls, a byte copy-out and a compare. The design states its reason and concedes the copy is legal C++, so this is a smallest-change judgment, not an error.

No -Wmissing-declarations and no compiler -Werror exists in CMakeLists.txt, src, t, cmake, nix, flake.nix, CMakePresets.json or GNUmakefile (the two -Werror hits are clang-format calls).
- Compile probe in the scratchpad (g++ -std=c++20 with tron's four warning flags): a definition of qk_rowmajor_128x4 whose first parameter is a struct instead of const bf16* compiles with exit 0 and no diagnostic. The same drift warns only under -Wmissing-declarations, which tron does not set.

Keep their current placement to avoid an extra test refactor") and does not carry the section-9 benefit claim [design-r4.txt:296]. The AMX-on row at :480 is consistent ("Compile real kernels and unconditional fake definitions").

Severity stays at note: an implementer builds the same thing either way. The only harm is a reader who believes the AMX-off Nix lane guards fake-versus-declaration agreement.
votes.correction:
Three narrowings; none changes the verdict.

1. Narrow "The AMX-off compile checks only class completeness." It also catches one drift class: a same-parameter definition whose return type or exception specification differs from the declaration is a compile error in every build (probe: g++ reports "ambiguating new declaration" for int qk_rowmajor_128x4(const bf16*, const bf16*, float*, size_t) against the void declaration). Only a parameter-list drift compiles silently. Suggested wording for design-r4.txt:559: "The AMX-off compile of the fakes checks class completeness and same-parameter return-type agreement only. The fakes stay where they are to avoid an extra test refactor. A parameter-list drift is caught only in the AMX-on configuration."

2. Say how the drift surfaces in the AMX-on link, so the recommendation is precise. With AMX on, the typed call in self_attention.hpp references a symbol the drifted fake no longer defines. The linker then pulls amx_attn.o out of the static libtron.a. That object defines all six functions in one translation unit [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@2880c3aa9b:76, :88, :98, :102, :122, :188, inside namespace tron::amx_attn_h128g4 at :28]. Its other five definitions collide with the remaining fakes, so the link fails with multiple-definition errors. "Caught only by the AMX-on link" is right; the mechanism is a multiple-definition error, not an undefined reference.

3. Fairness: the design's sentence echoes the round-3 lead note on G14, "Cost of the move: every AMX-off configuration, including the required Nix lane, stops compiling any kernel definition against the typed declarations" [r3-findings.md, G14 LEAD NOTE]. The three round-3 verifier corrections narrowed that cost to "not a functional loss" (source lens item 3), "checks nothing extra" (design-text lens item c) and "That lost check is small" (intent lens item b). Codex adopted the lead's framing rather than the corrections. State this so the finding reads as a wording fix, not a codex error.

Evidence nit: the finding lists self_attention.hpp :281-290 and :1531-1538 among the amx_attn_h128g4 uses. Both blocks are guarded by #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH, but neither names amx_attn_h128g4 (git grep at 2880c3aa9b). Cite them as guarded AMX blocks, not as kernel uses. The conclusion that every use is guarded is unchanged.

votes.correction: Three narrowings, none changing the verdict. (1) Fairness: the phrase echoes the round-3 lead note on G14 ("every AMX-off configuration ... stops compiling any kernel definition against the typed declarations") [r3-findings.md, G14 LEAD NOTE]; the round-3 design-text verifier narrowed it to "checks nothing extra" and the source lens to "only observable with AMX on", while the intent lens called the lost check "small" but asked the design to weigh it. Say that the wording originated in the review's own lead note and that the three round-3 lenses did not all say the same. (2) Keep one real benefit precise: at 8 lanes with AMX off, the fakes are the only instantiation of the packed class templates, because kv_cache.hpp uses the packed V owner only in 16-lane blocks [design-r4.txt:390] and the 8-lane row-major cache is retained [:297]; a by-value parameter in a definition forces completeness, so the fakes do check that the packed classes compile at 8 lanes. The fakes stay where they are to avoid an extra test refactor. A signature drift between a fake and its declaration is caught only by the AMX-on link." (3) Precision in the evidence sentence: the drift surfaces at the AMX-on link as a multiple-definition error, because the pulled-in amx_attn.o also defines available(), begin_region(), end_region() and pack_q_group_128x4() [src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp@2880c3aa9b:76-188], not merely because the object is pulled in. votes.correction: Narrow the claim in three places. (1) Replace "gives a benefit that does not exist" with "over-states the benefit". The AMX-off compile of the unconditional fakes does check three things against the header: (a) the by-value parameter classes are complete and instantiate at the fixed 64x128 shape in that build (g++: a definition with an incomplete by-value type is an error, a declaration is not; at 8 lanes the fakes are the only instantiation of the packed V view, because the cache uses the packed owner only in 16-lane blocks [design-r4.txt:389]); (b) the return type and the noexcept specifier agree with the declaration (g++ 11.4 errors: "has a different exception specifier", "ambiguating new declaration"); (c) the alias names and constants the fakes spell exist in the header. It does not check that the fake parameter lists match the declarations: a drifted fake is an unused overload, compiled with no warning under -Wall -Wextra. (2) Fix the attribution: the quote "checks nothing extra" is from the round-3 G14 design-text lens correction (c) only [r3-findings.md G14]; the source lens said "not a functional loss, because ... a signature mismatch is only observable with AMX on". Same substance, different words. (3) Reword the recommended replacement for design-r4.txt:559 to: "Keep class definitions complete in both vector widths. The AMX-off compile of the unconditional fakes checks only that their parameter classes are complete and that return type and noexcept match the declarations; a parameter-type drift compiles as an unused overload and surfaces only in an AMX-on link, where the static tron library pulls in the real amx_attn.o. The fakes keep their placement to avoid an extra test refactor [Build boundaries]." Add one observation: the section-9 cell carries a rationale that the body [:296] does not; under this round's rule that a Design response cell counts only if the body carries it, the cell should repeat the body's reason (the test-refactor cost) rather than introduce a new one. confirmed.title: Positive kernel-boundary checks must stay unevaluated; AMX-off t_llama_unit links no kernels
confirmed.section: 8 Behavior checks, Typed function boundaries row, design-r4.txt:465
confirmed.claim: The design places the typed-boundary checks in t_llama_unit and asks for positive checks that each kernel accepts its own view. t_llama_unit links tron and pos_fake only (t/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:586-592). With TRON_AMX_DISPATCH off, src/tron/kernels/amx_attn.cpp is not compiled, so libtron has no definition of qk_rowmajor_128x4 or weights_times_v_128x4. The declarations in amx_attn_iface.hpp are unconditional (no #if in that header). A positive check written as a real call would compile and then fail to link in the required 16-lane AMX-off configuration. A requires-expression inside STATIC_REQUIRE is unevaluated and does not ODR-use the function, so it links. The design names STATIC_REQUIRE but does not draw this consequence. It also does not say the checks must not run the kernels in the AMX-on build, where a real call outside a tile region would execute AMX code.
confirmed.design_quote: Positive checks accept each function's own view. Use STATIC_REQUIRE / STATIC_REQUIRE_FALSE for those call contracts

The central claim is that the design leaves the owner-to-view construction route open to three different implementations. The design text settles the route, once in section 2 and again through the rules of sections 5 and 8.

1. Section 2 retains the sketch's mechanism by name. Design-r4.txt:79 says "Retain: private packed storage, restricted construction of views, mutable-to-read-only conversion, typed kernel arguments, and optimized bulk operations." That bullet follows the paragraph on comment 5765866077 [design-r4.txt:75-77] and the sketch is linked from the same section. The sketch's "restricted construction of views" is one specific mechanism: `explicit vnni_view(T* data)` under `private:`, with `friend class vnni_tensor<Layout>;`, `friend struct detail::vnni_access;` and `template <typename, typename> friend class vnni_view;`, and `as_view() &` / `as_view() const &` building the view from `data_.data()` [github-review.json comments[3], sections 2-3]. A public constructor from a tagged type that still takes a pointer is a public raw-pointer constructor, which design-r4.txt:259 forbids. A public constructor from an owner reference would bypass the deleted rvalue forms of as_view() [design-r4.txt:250] and the "rvalue-owner views" rejection check [design-r4.txt:465]. The design says "Delete the separate helper entry points" [design-r4.txt:447] and "Remove or zero the save_k_helper< counts" [design-r4.txt:451]. The two harms the finding attaches to that sentence are both wrong, so the finding does not hold as a defect.

Harm 1, "deleting removes the only negative check that the helper entry point is gone from the generated code", is false on two counts. (a) The generator has exactly two save-call emit sites: "save_k_helper" at ingest/src/TronCpp.hs@30c4ac82cb:2338 and "save_k" at :2406. The design's next instruction, "Both save_k< counts become 2 calls" [design-r4.txt:451], requires both sites to emit `outer_state.template save_k<`. The text "save_k<" is not a substring of "save_k_helper<". So a leftover helper prefix at either site drops the save_k< count to 1 and fails the retained assertions at :2801 and :3225. The count-2 assertion is already a negative check for the helper prefix. (b) The design deletes both C++ helper overloads [h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2953 and :2962; design-r4.txt:447]. Any generated `save_k_helper<` call then fails the C++ build of the generated model code. A `shouldBe` 0 line would add only a guard against a hypothetical third generator site, caught earlier than the build.

Harm 2, "the two readings disagree with the count of seven", is false. The design's sentence is "Update all seven affected count and call-text assertions" [design-r4.txt:451]. Deleting an assertion is one way that assertion is affected. The design then lists what happens to each group: two save_k< counts, two save_k_helper< counts, two main-call tails, one helper-call prefix, and the unchanged :3232 [design-r4.txt:451]. That is 2 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 7 under either reading. "Deleting two of them leaves five edits, not seven" is the finding's own reframing of "affected" as "surviving", which the design does not say.

Both readings produce the same generated code and a passing spec. So the sentence is an option, not an ambiguity that changes the outcome. The option is also what round 3 asked for. The round-3 lead recommendation said "delete the save_k_helper< count line" [r3-findings.md:347], and the design-text verifier's corrected wording said "the save_k_helper< count line is deleted or set to 0" [r3-findings.md:350]. The round-4 lead recorded "save_k_helper< counts 0 (or deleted) ... The design's sentence matches (G23 applied)" [facts-r4.md:246-248]. Raising the two-option phrasing as a new defect re-litigates the wording the review itself supplied, without new evidence.

What survives is a style preference: the spec already uses explicit negative assertions (26 `shouldBe` False lines and one `shouldBe` 0 at LoopyTronSpec.hs@30c4ac82cb:2481), so "set to 0" matches convention. That is a preference, not a defect, and the design's existing safety net (bin/ingest-cabal test and the required "Test ingest" job, design-r4.txt:451) already catches any leftover assertion loudly.

The design's own sentence "bin/slice bench --check detects missing records, not stale timings" is right [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:1792-1832 reports coverage gaps and duplicate names only]. Constants confirmed: DRIFT_TEST_PCT = 0.30, DRIFT_MAKESPAN_PCT = 0.20 [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:115-116]; per-test drift skips records under 1.0 s [:3036-3038]. votes.reason:
The finding has two parts. Part 1 (label the deferral as a user exception) is true but has no consequence. Part 2 (name the drift warning as the Test host log symptom) is wrong on its central factual claim, and the recommended text would put an error into the design.

Part 1. The repository rules have no deferral clause; that is confirmed. t/AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:23-26 says to refresh config/test-benchmarks.json after adding or materially changing a test. .agents/skills/run-tron-tests/SKILL.md@2880c3aa9b:69-70 says such tests "require" bin/slice bench --new or --update. But the deferral wording in the design is exactly what the round-3 review asked for. The G26 intent-lens correction proposed the bullet text "refreshed on delphi-3bda under user direction, or the deferral and the user's direction are recorded in the PR description" [r3-findings.md, G26 VERIFIER CORRECTION (intent lens)]. The design-text correction proposed the same [r3-findings.md, G26 VERIFIER CORRECTION (design-text lens)]. The design now carries it at design-r4.txt:537 and repeats the user-direction requirement at :515 ("Bench requests the whole host ... so it requires user direction"). Whether the design calls this an "exception" or a "deferral with user direction" changes nothing an implementer does: user direction is required either way, and it is recorded in the PR either way. This part is a wording preference, not a defect that affects jhan's goal (an implementable parent PR that Ben accepts).

Part 2. The claim "bin/slice run prints 'Drift detected ...' when a test's measured duration differs from its record by more than 30 %" is true only with the -v/--verbose flag. emit_drift_warnings is called only under `if args.verbose:` [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:4554-4555]. The run subparser documents the flag as "show per-test (expected Ns) and the end-of-run drift report" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:6530-6533]. The CI Test host job runs the tron-test-host wrapper [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:573], and that wrapper executes `bin/slice run --filter=host` with no verbose flag [nix/tron-test-environment.nix@2880c3aa9b:31-34]. make test-host also passes no verbose flag [GNUmakefile@2880c3aa9b:905-906]. So the "Drift detected" line never appears in the Test host log, and the recommendation's sentence "bin/slice run prints 'Drift detected' in the Test host log" is false. The line that always appears is the summary "N passed, N skipped, N failed • makespan Xs expected Ys (speedup Zx)" [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:4545-4550]; it shows the expected total, not a per-test stale record. The design's existing sentence "bin/slice bench --check detects missing records, not stale timings" (design-r4.txt:537) stays correct [bin/slice@2880c3aa9b:1792-1832; facts-r4.md]. Nothing in the finding shows an implementer would build the wrong thing or that Ben would object.

Severity if the true part held alone: note. The finding is refuted because its only non-duplicate content (the Test host log symptom) is wrong.

findings_intro: Ten finders read the third revision through one lens each (C++ interface, behavior and arena construction, process and CI, handoff actionability, fidelity to Ben and jhan, simplicity and scope, formulas and page quality, the child's needs, a regression hunt over the round-3 to round-4 word diff, and a section-9 honesty audit). Their 46 candidates and 16 new defects the disposition checkers found in the fixes were merged into 46 candidates (16 duplicates folded, none dropped), and each was put to three verifiers who tried to refute it; a finding survived when at least two could not. questions_intro: Design section 2 carries the decision record: four questions for Ben (Q1 to Q4) with a proposed choice, a fallback if rejected and a record status, plus D5, the native-K typing scope jhan requested. All three judges found the record adequate. The table gives my reading of each row against Ben's three comments (evidence/github-review.json) and jhan's request.
questions_rows: Q1. May each concrete view contain its address formula? Proposed: yes; one view per layout, separate V and K owners, no layout-policy template.
Ben's sketch sections 1 and 2 and his reservation: "I'm not entirely convinced of the necessity of separate k_vnni_layout from vnni_view".

Adequate and unchanged since round 3. The paragraph under the table now states jhan's reading (the address formula belongs in the view) but no longer says it is right; J04 restores the verdict clause in one sentence.
Q2. Should const matrix and row objects prevent element mutation? Proposed: yes at both ranks.
Ben's sketch: "As with std::span, a const view object does not make its elements const. vnni_view<const bf16, Layout> does."
Adequate; the departure is flagged with a fallback. The row-conversion clause that round 3 asked for is now in the contract row (rows have no cross-constness conversion, :259).
Q3. May packed views expose logical rows through operator[]? Proposed: yes, a logical row expression with no public pointer; keep bounds-checked at().
Ben's review asked for the expr precedent; his sketch excluded operator[] because it suggests a contiguous row.
Adequate. The maintainer judge notes one phrase stronger than Ben's words survives at :439 ("the reviewer's uniform-expression requirement"; he wrote "I think the way I would approach this").
Q4. Is the smaller parent scope sufficient? Proposed: yes; expression reads and the existing typed bulk operations; slices, iterators and generic writes deferred.
Ben's review: "the usual operations that we expect of tensor types and, in particular, the row-wise load/store operations".

Adequate. append_v_row is now mapped to the sketch's V store_row (:266). One departure from the sketch is still stated nowhere: the row operations take tron's const_view and view where the sketch used std::span; the maintainer judge accepts it (the tron view carries the aligned and dma flags) but asks the page to say so, together with the sketch-name to design-name table round 3 requested.
D5. Who owns native-K typing? Requested scope: the issue author; reuse the existing K view type through the new const_native_k_view alias.
jhan's request and the issue title; not part of Ben's sketch.
Right, and the round-3 wording slip is fixed ("the new const_native_k_view alias"). G35 notes that section 2 still alternates between issue author and assignee for the same person.
The sketch-name to design-name table (round-3 maintainer ask), the std::span departure, and the CI route to execution evidence.
The first two are one table and one sentence for Ben's benefit. The third is J01, the one item that gates the implementer, and belongs in section 8, not in the record.

verdict_intro: Three judges read the design and the review summary independently. All three give accept with minor edits and say the design is implementable now; all three find the decision record adequate. The implementing agent would build steps 1 to 6 from the page and stop once, at the first test commit, on the CI route (J01). judges.label: Implementing agent's view
judges.reasons: I could start building the parent from this page today and would stop exactly once, at step 7, to ask how to trigger the required Test host job. Steps 1 to 6 are specified at the mechanism level and every load-bearing claim I checked against the pinned source held. The forward declarations at design-r4.txt:243-245 match the existing types: the whole-plane page::k overloads return kv_block::k_view() (kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1549-1569, :2208-2219), whose default stride row_major<seq<R,C>> is sseq<C,1> (seq.hpp@2880c3aa9b:388-394, :509-511), so const_native_k_view<64,128> is the same type and the qk_rowmajor_128x4 call at self_attention.hpp:1653-1655 can pass pg.template k<geometry.kv>(slot, kv_head) as :280 says. seq and sseq are aliases (seq.hpp:22, :25), so the rule at :299 is right. The page-level kv_block_at_storage<geometry>(offset, kv_head) that :284 names exists (kv_cache.hpp:1855-1863). The scaled_v_expr access route, the arena construction, the bf16_chunk fallback, the extraction pattern and the fixture migration are each stated once and consistently (:258, :260, :262, :286, :366-368, :397-403); facts-r4.md confirms each against source. Two mechanism gaps exist but a compiler surfaces both: page::scaled_v is one width-neutral body passing .v[0] to both constructors (kv_cache.hpp:2252-2262), so it needs a width branch the design does not mention; and the 16 raw-pointer set_v callers (t_llama_unit.cpp:142, 796, 1554, 1723, 1923, 2533, 2535, 2568, 2569, 2690, 2705, 2721, 2792, 2802; t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp:98; heterogeneous_scheduler_compile.cpp:443) are not listed, although their sources are already 64-byte aligned (for example :134 alignas(64), :1711 btensor). One factual slip sits on the production write path: :270 says the model source already has a view with dma = false, but vs is a btensor (btensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:21 = dmatensor<bf16,...>) whose as_view() carries dma = true (dmatensor.hpp@2880c3aa9b:223-228); the flag is provenance only (views.hpp@2880c3aa9b:11-19) and append_v_row deduces Dma (:266), so the wrong value cannot produce wrong bytes, but the sentence must be corrected. The one place I would stop is the evidence rule at :495-497: the design demands a required GCP Nix Test host run for the parent, forbids the Run CI label without direction (:167, :495), and says the parent must pass the AMX-on local gate before it leaves draft (:485, :536), yet a draft PR runs no product job: the Build ingest, Build model traces and Prepare Tron build inputs jobs carry an if that requires a non-draft PR or the Run CI label (gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:3-9, :34-37, :46-49, :57-60), and Test host depends on them. The repository rule allows the parent to be ready for review (AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:5-6) and ready_for_review is a trigger event (gcp-nix.yml:13-14), so the route exists, but the design never names it; an implementing agent either stops to ask or asks for the label the design forbids. The six partly items (G15, G35, G17, H01, G46, G41) are wording and citation gaps that do not change what gets built; G41 is the same fact as the :270 correction. The 47 new findings contain one major (J01, the route above), the rest are minors and notes that the compiler, the linker or the section-9 bookkeeping catch. This is a lighter round than round 3, where the G01 ambiguity produced two possible PR shapes; nothing in this revision does that.

judges.label: Maintainer's (Ben's) view
judges.reasons: The design answers all three of my comments, and the two interface gaps I refused to let implementation start with in round 3 are closed in the body text. Comment 1 (r4065141577, the worker index) is answered at design-r4.txt:447-451. The child has two save_k overload pairs and two save_k_helper overload pairs (save_k is the model's K-save function; the pairs are at h/tron/models/model.hpp@30c4ac82cb:2953, 2962, 3065 and 3073, one pair keyed by an operation index and one by an attention_operation_descriptor). The design merges them into one save_k(..., worker_ix = 0, n_workers = 1) and deletes the helper entry points [design-r4.txt:447]. That is exactly what I asked for. Comment 2 (review 5270587330) asked for an expr-based packed tensor with row-wise load and store operations. The design gives v_vnni_view and v_vnni_row that inherit expr [design-r4.txt:251], the operations append_v_row, load_row and copy_token [design-r4.txt:267-273], and typed cache-plane arguments on both AMX kernels [design-r4.txt:290]. Comment 3 (my sketch, 5765866077) is followed on every point I would insist on: one aligned array owner with lvalue-only as_view() [design-r4.txt:249-250]; private pointer construction with mutable-to-const conversion only and no public pointer route [design-r4.txt:259]; bounds-checked at() using repository assertions [design-r4.txt:257]; the arena constructs the real storage type by array placement-new, never casts the old SIMD array, and adds no clearing [design-r4.txt:361-369]; k_storage selected by std::conditional_t [design-r4.txt:426]; page accessors that return typed views [design-r4.txt:284, :431]; store_block keeping the masked 16-token transpose path [design-r4.txt:433]; the AVX-512 fallback qk_group taking the typed view [design-r4.txt:434]. Round-3 must-fix 1 is settled the way my sketch allows: detail::scaled_v_expr (the V weighted-sum expression in kv_cache.hpp) is named a permitted SIMD user of detail::v_vnni_access, obtains the pair-tile base once, and keeps its _mm512_load_si512 and _mm512_dpbf16_ps loop [design-r4.txt:260, :286, :346, :390]. Round-3 must-fix 2 is settled: the t_amx_numerics PV case holds its page in a v_vnni_tensor<64,128> owner (16,384 bytes, 64-byte aligned), fills it with 64 append_v_row calls, and passes owner.as_view() [design-r4.txt:399-401]. Round-3 must-fix 3 is settled: D5 now says the alias const_native_k_view is new and the view type is existing [design-r4.txt:106]. Nothing is attributed to me that I did not write. The comment ids and times match the saved JSON (18:24:52; 18:53:47; 18:58:31 edited 18:59:58 UTC) [design-r4.txt:73-75; evidence/github-review.json]. "The reviewer expressed doubt about that separation, rather than a final decision" [design-r4.txt:77] matches my "not entirely convinced of the necessity of separate k_vnni_layout from vnni_view". Q2's "span-like const rule" and Q3's "excluded indexing because it suggests a contiguous row" match my sketch text [design-r4.txt:103-104]. Lines 301 and 416 correctly say my header was h/tron/tensor/vnni.hpp. One phrase is still stronger than my words: "the reviewer's uniform-expression requirement" [design-r4.txt:439]; I wrote "I think the way I would approach this". judges.label: Risk reviewer's view
judges.reasons: The behavior rules that could silently corrupt data are stated and match source. The NaN table is right: fp32 0x7F800001 truncates to bf16 0x7F80 (+infinity) in the packed append, and the generic conversion gives 0x7F81 (a NaN) only without TRON_IGNORE_NAN, the macro every non-Debug build defines [design-r4.txt:349-352; h/common/numerics/bf16.hpp@f46e48ba:92-109; src/tron/CMakeLists.txt@2880c3aa9b:292-295]. The padding rule is stated as an operation sequence: an even append zeros its odd partner without reading, an odd append merges into an initialized pair, and direct element writes do neither [design-r4.txt:266-267, :319-325]. The inherited bf16_chunk fallback preserves stored bits, because a widened bf16 has a zero low half and fp32s_to_bf16s changes only NaNs with nonzero low bits [design-r4.txt:258; h/tron/kernels/expr.hpp@2880c3aa9b:110-116]. The aligned destination view of load_row adds no fault risk: today's get_v already stores with _mm512_store_ps and _mm256_store_si256, which require alignment, and every existing destination is 64-byte aligned (alignas(64) arrays at t/t_llama_unit.cpp@2880c3aa9b:807, :1563, :2026, :2749, :2812; tensor<head_size> at :2538; the GOF scratch at src/tron/gof.cpp@2880c3aa9b:203) [design-r4.txt:268-270; h/tron/models/kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:2421-2431, :2454-2463]. Object lifetime is low risk: the array placement-new form is the one that does not clear storage [design-r4.txt:359-364], the helper runs inside allocate_kv_group after the arena is installed [design-r4.txt:365], and every member it needs (n_pages, support_eagle_, storage_slot_count_) is set in the constructor's initializer list before that call, storage_view_offset_ has a default member initializer, and slot_base returns nullptr for an absent arena [kv_cache.hpp@2880c3aa9b:1091-1103, :1129, :1188-1197, :963-973]. The design also demands an inspection of the optimized allocation and restore code for clearing loops [design-r4.txt:372]. Concurrency is unchanged for the parent: pair writes stay sequential and adjust_grains_for_partners stays in model.hpp [design-r4.txt:326-327]; the one-lane-per-line K rule is child scope [design-r4.txt:436]. Process rules are right: stack rule, Skip benchmarks, no Run CI, retarget before pushing the child's new history, cost records under authorization [design-r4.txt:165, :411, :420, :537]. The one consequential gap is CI (J01 with J36). A draft pull request runs only the lint, machinery and fresh-plan jobs; the product pipeline (Build ingest through Test host) needs a non-draft PR or the Run CI label [.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:5, :168-171, :294-297, :382-385]. The design requires required-suite execution evidence before committing a new test, forbids the label, and wants per-case Catch2 lines from Slice logs that stay on a runner the implementer usually cannot reach [design-r4.txt:495, :500-504; AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:19-24]. It never names the route that satisfies all of these: the parent is the PR based on main and may leave draft [AGENTS.md@2880c3aa9b:12-13; design-r4.txt:165], and the ready_for_review event runs the product pipeline [gcp-nix.yml@2880c3aa9b:13]. The consequence is a stalled PR or a needless exception request, not a wrong build, so this is a text fix and not a redo. The compile-surface omissions (L01: the set_v raw-pointer call in the template exercise_page at t/t_amx_dispatch_dtype.cpp@2880c3aa9b:98 is instantiated only under #ifdef TRON_AMX_DISPATCH at :192-207; L02: page::scaled_v needs a width branch; L03: positive kernel checks must stay unevaluated) fail only in the AMX-on build, which the design already requires to compile before the parent leaves draft [design-r4.txt:481, :536]. The six partly items (G15, G35, G17, H01, G46, G41) are wording or child-scope precision, and none changes what the parent's code does.

verdict_outro: What changed since round 3. Round 3 had one design major (G01, where scaled_v_expr obtains the packed address) and two items two judges refused to start without (G22, the numerics fixture route; G09, the constraint mechanism). All three are resolved in the body with every fact checked. The round-3 partly count fell from 25 to 8. This round's one major is a process paragraph the design's own rules require; none of the 47 findings changes what gets built, and the checkers found no regression among the 79 known items. Four minors are wording on the production path or the record (J09, J04, J05, J06); the rest are mechanism sentences a compiler would otherwise surface (L02, J07, J12) or bookkeeping (J15).

What the design does not have to do. It compiled nothing and ran nothing; it posted nothing and edited no issue; sw-dev-01 is codex's user rule; main moving by one line since 2880c3aa9b is covered by its relocate rule. None of those is a finding. Ben's answers to Q1 to Q4 are not needed to start: the design says to implement the proposed choices and label them Proposed in the PR description, and all three judges accept that.
rejected_intro: These candidates were refuted by at least two of the three verifiers, or dropped by the lead after reading the votes. They are listed so a reader can see what was considered and why it did not hold; the votes page carries the full reasons.
method: This round used the round-3 shape. The lead first re-verified the facts the new text relies on (the self_attention.hpp block range, the panel formula against k_vnni::index, the seven LoopyTronSpec assertions, the Slice log path and retention, the lint-toolchain check, the child's 8-lane guard, the three cost-record rows, the fixture lines of t_amx_numerics) against the pinned commits and refreshed the live state of main, issue #4525, PR 4424 and PR 4505; that record is evidence/claude-review-r4/lead-verified-facts-r4.md. Two of the lead's pre-round facts were wrong and are corrected below.

Numbers of this round: 216 agents, 26.3 million tokens, 2 hours 7 minutes; 17 disposition batches (51 agents), 10 finders, 1 merge agent, 46 merged candidates with 138 verifier votes, 1 critic with 4 candidates and 12 votes, 3 judges. The workflow result is evidence/claude-review-r4/workflow-result.json; the inner result (the script's return value) is workflow-result-inner.json.
method_bullets: Dispositions: 17 batches of 3 to 6 items; per batch one checker and two re-graders (source-truth, fairness); majority of three; batch files in evidence/claude-review-r4/batches/, built from the round-3 findings by build_inputs.py.

New findings: 10 finders (the same ten lenses as round 3, with the regression hunt over the round-3 to round-4 word diff and the section-9 audit over the four disposition tables), plus 16 new defects the checkers found in the fixes; one merge agent deduplicated; three verifiers (source, design-text fairness, intent) per candidate; a finding survived when at least two could not refute it; the lead read every vote before grading and folded the corrections into the recommendations.

Completeness critic after verification; its four candidates went through the same three verifiers. The critic also disputed the lead's facts file (see the next bullet) and the severity of J08, which the lead accepted.

Lead errors corrected: (1) lead-verified-facts-r4.md called the design's sentence at :270 defensible on the strength of the round-3 G41 lead note (dma = false); the production V buffer is hardware::btensor, a dmatensor with dma = true, so the sentence is wrong (J09) and the facts file now carries a correction block. (2) The same file named t_llama_unit.cpp:819 and :2038 as the bf16 get_v callers; the bf16 callers are :819 and :1575, and :2038 is a float caller (J37). (3) The round-3 facts file gave the self_attention.hpp width-check block as 31-37; it is 30-36, as the design says.
Three judges (implementer, maintainer, risk) read the design and the review summary independently.

Limits: no code was compiled or run; no chromium on this host, so the page was checked structurally (ASCII, anchors, links) and not rendered; the Test host runner measurement (J36) is a read-only GitHub API sample of the most recent runs, not a full history; agents can make mistakes, so every finding carries its evidence and votes; the lead's own reading is not a substitute for Ben's.
